## What Is a GLP-1?

Glucagon-like petide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists belong to a class of prescription medications that are primarily used to treat type 2 diabetes and obesity. They help lower glucose levels and manage metabolism.

“GLP-1 medications mimic a natural hormone released after eating,” explains Sarah Velayati, M.D., assistant professor in the Albert Einstein College of Medicine at Montefiore Einstein Medical Center, adding that these medications can help you feel—and stay— full more quickly and for longer periods.

“Many patients experience meaningful weight loss, often around 10% to 20% of their total body weight over time, along with improvements in blood pressure, cholesterol levels and diabetes control,” she says.

Some GLP-1 medications are only approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat type 2 diabetes, while others are also approved for weight management in individuals with obesity or those with overweight and at least one weight-related condition, in conjunction with reduced calorie intake and exercise. Compounded GLP-1 medications have also become increasingly available, but these medications come with risks, as they are not evaluated by the FDA.

* * *

## Types of GLP-1 Medications

While commonly referred to as just GLP-1s, there are single GLP-1 agonists, and then there are dual GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonists, notes Peter Balazs, M.D., a board-certified obstetrician and gynecologist and hormone and weight loss specialist at Hormone and Weight Loss Doctors of NJ, with offices in New York and New Jersey.

While the GLP-1 helps to reduce “food noise” and increase satiety, “the GIP component increases fat oxidation, helping the body burn fat more efficiently, and clinical trials have shown that it significantly reduces calorie intake at meals,” notes Dr. Balazs. “This dual action makes it the most effective pharmacotherapy to date, with an average weight loss of 15% to 21% of body weight.”

Common [GLP-1s](https://www.forbes.com/health/weight-loss/approved-weight-loss-medication/) approved for chronic weight management by the FDA include injectable and oral [Wegovy](https://www.forbes.com/health/weight-loss/wegovy/) ([semaglutide](https://www.forbes.com/health/weight-loss/semaglutide/)) and injectable [Saxenda](https://www.forbes.com/health/weight-loss/saxenda-for-weight-loss/) (liraglutide), as well as the dual agonist injectable medication [Zepbound](https://www.forbes.com/health/weight-loss/zepbound-fda-approved-what-to-know/) (tirzepatide).

- **Injectable medications.** Injectable GLP-1 medications may come in single-use pens, like the Zepbound pen or Wegovy pen, multi-dose pens, such as the Zepbound KwikPen, or single-use vials. These are typically injected once weekly.
- **Oral medications:** FDA- approved oral GLP-1 medications include the Foundayo (orforglipron) tablet, taken once daily, and the Wegovy (semaglutide) tablet, also taken once daily.
- **Compounded alternatives.** “Compounded GLP-1 medications vary in potency, dosage and have potential for impurities,” says [John Morton, M.D.](https://www.forbes.com/health/medical-advisory-board/john-morton-m-d-m-p-h/), the system lead for surgical quality and bariatric services in the Yale New Haven Health System of six hospitals and Forbes Health Advisory Board member. Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved and can come with risks as they are not reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality.

## What to Consider When Choosing Between Affordable GLP-1 Options

“Always prioritize safety and evidence by ensuring thorough pre-treatment evaluation, slow dose titration and a long-term follow-up plan,” urges Dr. Balazs.

When it comes to choosing an affordable GLP-1, [cost](https://www.forbes.com/health/weight-loss/glp-1-costs/) is typically a major factor. In some cases, the cost of GLP-1 medications can be covered by insurance, notes Dr. Morton. “Direct-to-patient programs exist for both Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly,” he adds, which may offer savings for those utilizing self-pay.

As for lower-cost alternatives to brand-name or [FDA-approved weight loss medications](https://www.forbes.com/health/weight-loss/approved-weight-loss-medication/), Dr. Morton considers compounded GLP-1 medications a red flag. “Patients should not compromise \[on\] cost, convenience or quality,” he says.

“With the rise of online prescribing, it is important to be cautious,” adds Dr. Velayati.

“Patients should look for providers who perform a thorough medical evaluation (not just a quick form) and who order appropriate labs,” she explains, adding that support should involve access to clinicians when necessary and follow-up appointments.

“Providers should clearly discuss risks, benefits and expectations,” she continues. “Be cautious of services that offer quick prescriptions, unusually low prices or no follow-up.”
